newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P rates Bank Negara Indonesia BBB/A-3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P rates Bank Negara Indonesia BBB/A-3.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said it assigned long-term and short-term counterparty ratings to PT Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) of BBB and A-3 respectively.
The ratings outlook is stable, it said.
S&P said its ratings were assigned on the basis of the bank's stand-alone risk profile and the probable support of the Indonesian government, BNI's owner, if the bank became financially distressed.
"The ratings fully reflects BNI's credit characteristics and are not constrained specifically by Indonesia's local currency rating of A-plus and foreign currency rating of BBB," it said.
BNI is Indonesia's largest bank with about a 10 percent market share of commercial banking assets as at end-1995.
It has an established brand name, is well regarded locally and has an intangible marketing advantage, S&P said.
BNI's capitalisation is reasonable with satsiafctory equity-to-assets and risk-adjusted capital ratios, S&P said.

While its financial profile is dampened by low-to-moderate profitability and moderately high non-performing loans, its strengthened fiscal health in 1995 allowed BNI to be one of the few state-owned banks to increase market share, it said.

BNI's non-performing loans level is better than those of many other state banks but higher than many private sector banks and its large lending exposures are believed to be high relative to internatiional peers, although within central bank guidelines, it said.

Although the government does not guarantee BNI's debt, the bank's origins in the war of independence and relationship with the government enhances the bank's risk profile given the context of Indonesia's socio-economic realities, S&P said.

BNI will be the first state bank to make an initial public offering on the Jakarta Stock Exchange and the potential for a reduced state stake has been factored into the ratings. Current laws prevent dilution of state ownership below 51 percent.
The partial float is likely to strengthen the bank's financial flexibility, S&P said.
